claims.text: StandardShipping.ForOrder returns 0 when totalVnd >= 2_000_000 and 30_000 otherwise.
StandardShippingIsFreeFromTwoMillion creates a StandardShipping and asserts ForOrder(1_999_999) == 30_000 and ForOrder(2_000_000) == 0.
EveryKindAnswersTheSameCall also calls ForOrder(2_000_000) on a StandardShipping and expects 0, so changing the limit to 2_500_000 makes both ShippingFeeTests fail.
`dotnet test <project> --filter ShippingFeeTests` builds the test project and runs only tests whose fully qualified name contains ShippingFeeTests, then reports passed and failed counts.

claims.text: A unit test checks one piece of code in isolation; a check that goes through a database, files or network is a different kind of test even if it is fast.
A test with 1_999_999 and 2_000_000 would catch > written in place of >= in StandardShipping.
Unit tests usually run in milliseconds and are repeatable: they give the same result on every run while the code is unchanged.
Arrange-act-assert is a common pattern for structuring a unit test.
